name: Squirrel Bait
label: Homestead
lede: Five Louisville high schoolers played roughly two dozen shows, made one EP and one LP, and split up before most of them could legally buy a drink. Slint, Bastro and Gastr del Sol grew out of the wreckage.

eras.title: Halloween in Louisville
eras.text: Two high school friends start a hardcore trio. Then come new drummers, a singer and a second guitarist, and the band stops sounding like hardcore.

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait · Wikipedia: David Grubbs · Popdose
years.h: Halloween night, and Squirrelbait Youth plays its first show
years.p: [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] on guitar and vocals, Clark Johnson on bass and Rich Schuler on drums play fast hardcore in Louisville. A demo tape under that name follows the same year.
years.xp:
Grubbs and Johnson were high school friends. Grubbs had already put out a four-song 7" called With Illustrations in 1982 with an earlier band, the Happy Cadavers.

On the name, Grubbs told Popdose: "It really was not a reference to testicles! Scout's honor!"

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait · Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait (EP)
years.h: A new singer, and the band stops sounding like hardcore
years.p: [[Peter Searcy|52b1ea1e-34de-4fca-aae9-35144e885d7d]] takes over vocals, [[Britt Walford|7fde6efa-750a-49c1-abee-7767230407ff]] replaces the original drummer and [[Brian McMahan|bebfec95-35a3-4cc8-b85e-8b178d09526d]] adds the second guitar. Three songs from the 1984 demo end up on the band's records.
years.xp: This is the line-up that made the records, give or take one drummer swap: Ben Daughtrey would replace Walford before the debut came out. Walford and McMahan would go on to start [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] together.

eras.title: Opening for Hüsker Dü, with Albini's logo on the flyer
eras.text: The band opens for the bands it worships, gets an offer from Bob Mould's label, and ends up on Homestead with a debut EP.

years.cap: Peter Searcy singing, a guitarist beside him, in a still from 1985 live footage
years.src: Vice: We Talk to Squirrel Bait · Popdose: The Popdose Interview
years.h: Opening for Hüsker Dü, in front of 500 to 600 people
years.p: At the Jockey Club in Newport, across the river from Cincinnati, Squirrel Bait plays "Sun God". The tape is the only live video of the band that Grubbs knows of.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Vice it was "one of the most incredible nights of my life". Kids drove in from Louisville, Lexington, Indianapolis and Columbus, and the band played the Jockey Club four times in all, once on a bill with the Meat Puppets.

The footage also caught a punk from Lexington who interrupted the set to yell at the crowd, after what Grubbs says was a rough time in the pit. Popdose lists the ages on stage: Grubbs 17, Johnson 18, Daughtrey 19 and McMahan 16.

Hüsker Dü's Bob Mould and Grant Hart offered to put out the band's record on their label, Reflex.

years.cap: Flyer for Big Black, Urge Overkill and Squirrel Bait, Jockey Club, May 26, 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait (EP) · Popdose: The Popdose Interview
years.h: The EP comes out on Homestead, with a logo from Steve Albini
years.p: Squirrel Bait has eight songs, recorded with Howie Gano at Sound on Sound in Crestwood, Kentucky. Big Black and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]] had pushed the band on Homestead.
years.xp:
Grubbs told Popdose that "we couldn't have been more thrilled" by the Reflex offer, but the band went with Homestead. Spin's John Leland wrote that the record "doesn't just assault you. It consumes you."

Ben Daughtrey took over from Walford on drums before release, and two songs came from earlier demo sessions. Per Popdose, Steve Albini spray-painted the band's name on a flyer for a Squirrel Bait, Urge Overkill and Big Black show at the Jockey Club, and it became the logo. The Shins later recreated the cover for their "New Slang" video.

Grubbs and Johnson left for college in summer 1985, and Popdose has the band splitting up then before re-forming.

eras.title: One more summer, then Skag Heaven
eras.text: Grubbs and Johnson come home from college for a tour and a record. By the end of it, the next bands are already forming.

years.src: Wikipedia: Skag Heaven · Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait
years.p: "Kid Dynamite" and "Slake Train Coming" come out as a single on Homestead. Both then go onto Skag Heaven, because the band had only eight songs and wanted a longer record than the EP.

yt: Full set, 7th St. Entry, Minneapolis, Aug 8, 1986
years.h: Summer 1986 on the road, trying out new songs each night
years.p: Grubbs and Johnson come home from college to open for [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]] and [[Volcano Suns|4837e8d3-a13f-4670-9684-82970411f4bc]].
years.xp:
In August the band recorded Skag Heaven with Howie Gano at Sound on Sound, then Grubbs and Johnson went back to school.

A 47-minute set at the 7th St. Entry in Minneapolis on August 8, 1986 survives on video, and so does a 37-minute set two nights later at Exit in Chicago.

years.p: Britt Walford and Brian McMahan carry on together in Louisville and form Slint with David Pajo, who came from the band Maurice.

years.cap: All five members around a Volkswagen Beetle
years.src: Wikipedia: Skag Heaven · Agit Reader: Past Perfect
years.h: Skag Heaven runs 25 minutes and 46 seconds
years.p: Homestead releases the LP, which closes on a cover of Phil Ochs's "Tape from California". "Too Close to the Fire" is the only song Searcy wrote alone.
years.xp:
The Agit Reader notes that all five members were still in high school when it was made. Daughtrey designed the cover and Guy Dove took the photograph. "Rose Island Road" is named for a winding country road that meant something to the band, and the road turns up again on Slint's album cover.

Wikipedia lists ten songs on the LP, two of them from the earlier "Kid Dynamite" single.

years.p: David Grubbs and Clark Johnson form the trio with drummer John McEntire.

eras.title: The family tree
eras.text: Squirrel Bait ends for good, and its members spend the next decade becoming the reason anyone asks about it.

years.big: "I wouldn't describe it as amicable, but not so toxic either."
q: I wouldn't describe it as amicable, but not so toxic either.
years.p: Grubbs, to Popdose, on the split he dates to summer 1986. Wikipedia blames artistic tensions and members leaving for higher education; Johnson goes into law in Louisville.

years.src: Wikipedia: Peter Searcy · Agit Reader: Past Perfect
years.h: Searcy fronts Big Wheel for four years
years.p: [[Peter Searcy|52b1ea1e-34de-4fca-aae9-35144e885d7d]] plays with Big Wheel from 1989 to 1993 and makes three albums, two on Mammoth. Before that, he and Ben Daughtrey had a funk-rock band, Fanci Pantz.
years.xp: Fanci Pantz drew label interest but broke up before making an album, according to Wikipedia.

years.p: [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] release Tweez on Jennifer Hartman Records, recorded by Steve Albini in fall 1987. It's the debut from the band Walford and McMahan started after Squirrel Bait.

years.h: Spiderland becomes the record people cite
years.p: McMahan and Walford's second album for Touch and Go, recorded live in Chicago with producer Brian Paulson, is where fans trace post-rock back to.
years.xp: Wikipedia says McMahan visited Paulson in Minneapolis during the sessions for Bastro's last album, Sing the Troubled Beast, and was in a near-fatal car accident.

years.h: Grubbs moves to Chicago, and Bastro becomes Gastr del Sol
years.p: Grubbs goes to graduate school at the University of Chicago. [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] joins as a partner after the first album, per Grubbs's Wikipedia page.

years.src: Wikipedia: Squirrel Bait · Wikipedia: David Grubbs
years.p: Grubbs puts it out on Dexter's Cigar, the Drag City imprint he co-runs. The Homestead recordings were later gathered onto a single CD.
